feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. Iteration 8 (0.6 kg, with the iteration 5 layout and controller) is the best measured design at 257.45: oval progress 0.89, 10 of 20 oval finishes, zero line losses, and max_error 0.0603 m on s-bend and 0.0615 m on slalom. Iteration 9 (0.5 kg, otherwise identical) scored 81.24, with oval progress 0.27 and no finishes, so mass below 0.6 kg is a cliff and the trend has reversed. Iteration 5 (0.8 kg) was lower at 151.9. Iterations 3, 4, 6 and 7 rejected the 0.10 m track, y 0.06 m, the 16 mm footprint and the inner ±0.04 m spacing, and all four cut oval progress. Answering your gain question: edge drift at about 0.060 m with zero losses across all three tracks is a controller-response limit, not a sensor limit. Body width cannot raise the 0.06 m off-track floor. If the next race reproduces iteration 8 (oval finishes near 10 of 20, max_error near 0.060 m, zero losses), the geometry is settled and the remaining gains are the controller's job. If oval progress falls below 0.5 at 0.6 kg, the controller or seed is the cause, so keep 0.6 kg and do not retry mass below it. If line losses appear on any track, revert to the layout in iteration 5.
requested_changes: Keep mass at 0.6 kg with the iteration 8 layout (outer ±0.06 m, inner ±0.03 m, y 0.04 m, 12 mm footprints, 0.12 m track, 0.03 m radius). Iteration 8 gave 257.45 and iteration 9 showed 0.5 kg collapses oval progress to 0.27.

Only if the next race reproduces iteration 8 (oval finishes at about 10 of 20, zero line losses), try one small mass step of 0.55 kg. This is a measured bracket between the 0.6 kg best and the 0.5 kg cliff, and the expected gain is smaller drift on s-bend and slalom (max_error below 0.060 m). Revert to 0.6 kg if oval progress falls below 0.8.

Do not retry inner ±0.04 m (iteration 7 oval progress 0.22), sensor_size 0.016 m (iteration 6 oval progress 0.51), wheel_track 0.10 m (iteration 3 oval progress 0.14) or y 0.06 m (iteration 4 oval progress 0.20). Each was rejected by earlier evidence.
